text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- The consolidation of the Gdynia and Szczecin shipyards and the Poznan-based Hipolit Cegielski ship engine maker in a shipyard holding will start in the first quarter of 1997, industry and trade deputy minister Tadeusz Soroka said.

- Poland's state treasury, the Gorzow province governor and city authorities of Kostrzyn and Slubice are shareholders in a firm formed to run the Kostrzyn Slubice Special Economic Zone. The company's capital is 450,000 zlotys.
- The privatisation of Telekomunikacja Polska SA, the monopolist telecom operator, should start next year, government officials said.
- Poland's insurance firms will be allowed to invest part of their funds abroad as of January 1, 1997, the finance ministry said.
- The Tychy municipality, southern Poland, will probably issue municipal bonds in 1998, its financial director Helena Szarkowska said.

- The Warsaw-based Bank Handlowy Capital Operations Centre (BH COK) and the Gospodarczy Bank Wielkopolski SA (GBW SA) will organise a bond issue of the Gorzow Wielkopolski municipality worth 20 million zlotys.

- Poland's Opole province and Germany's Rhineland Palatinate have set up an economic cooperation office in Opole, southwestern Poland. The office will assist contacts between Polish and German firms, provide legal assistance and carry out market research, the Rhineland Palatinate state secretary for economy, agriculture and transport Gunter Eymael said.
NOWA EUROPA

- The listed Polisa insurance firm will trade a part of its shares on the recently started over-the-counter (OTC) market and will be the first firm to trade its stock on the Warsaw bourse and the OTC market.
- The Gdansk-based Stocznia Remontowa shipyard will construct an 83 metre long, 71 metre wide and 32 metre high catamaran vessel contracted by Norway's Neptun Heavy Lift AS.
- The Lublin-based Resta office file maker has received an International Standards Organisation (ISO)-9001 quality product certificate awarded by the German RW TUV firm.

- The listed Stomil Olsztyn tyre company, which carried out various environment related investments in the last five years, has been declared an environment friendly plant following seasonal air quality checks conducted by the provincial environment protection inspectorate.

- Leading international consulting firms have been carrying out research for Japan's Toyota automaker in Silesia, southern Poland and in the north of the Czech Republic, related to the future location of the concern's car plant in central Europe.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- The average monthly salary in Poland's corporate sector in October this year was 1,017 zlotys, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.
ZYCIE

- The treasury ministry state secretary for privatisation Wieslaw Kaczmarek will not dismiss the KGHM copper combine's board member Ireneusz Nawrocki whose removal has been demanded by the Solidarity union. Kaczmarek defended him as a qualified professional who avoided confrontation.
PARKIET

- The listed ComputerLand software firm has tendered successfully for computer equipment delivery and maintenance services' provision to tax offices around Poland worth 3.35 million zlotys, the finance ministry said.

- The PZL Debica refrigeration equipment maker has generated operational profit for the first time in three years, it said. Following restructuring the plant's output in the first three quarters of 1996 was 22 percent higher than in the same period last year.
